title: Mark the implemented mask safeguards as complete
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mark the implemented mask safeguards as complete**

In this commit, none of the six items under this heading remains an unimplemented blocker: the committed DLL exports ordinal 100, `_ShowVV2AppearanceChooser@12`, `Vv2MaskRestore`, and `Vv2MaskSaveSidecar`; `build_vv2_mask_stage2.py` captures the save slot and saves after sweep clearing; the companion compares materialized appearance values before charging and stages a fully verified atlas through a temporary file; and the atlas builder already derives its source path from `__file__`. Presenting these completed safeguards as current defects will send a future integrator toward unnecessary or conflicting rework, so this section should record them as satisfied invariants rather than blockers.

body:

title: Do not reconcile population exceeding occupancy
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not reconcile population exceeding occupancy**

Under the definition established immediately above, every living villager must occupy a record, while skeletons can only make the occupied count larger than the living count. A reading of 15 occupied records against a HUD population of 18 therefore cannot be explained by distinguishing occupancy from population; it instead indicates a mismatched scan, timing, pool, or HUD definition that still needs investigation. Recording it as reconciled preserves a logically impossible conclusion.

title: Correct the claim that VV2 masks are outside the shipped catalog
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Correct the claim that VV2 masks are outside the shipped catalog**

`load_fun_patches()` actually returns `vv2_enable_origins_exclusive_features`: `data/vv2_origins_feature.json` is enabled, catalog-visible, and contains the `.mtab`/`.vvmk` save-slot, render, sweep, and atlas hooks. Therefore a normal catalog selection of VV2 Origins does apply this runtime, contrary to the statement that patcher output is unaffected. This false containment claim is especially misleading because it is also used to justify closing user-impact review threads.

title: Verify the charge before applying the warp
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the charge before applying the warp**

When the charge routine rejects or alters the deduction, or the balance changes while the companion's confirmation is open, this call happens only after `ShowVv5TimeWarp` has already changed the clock and villager ages and displayed success. The subsequent balance comparison merely routes to `charge_unknown`; it cannot undo the warp and even displays text claiming the clock was not changed. Fresh evidence in this revision is that the new balance read at line 2145 precedes the companion's blocking `MessageBoxA`, while this charge remains after the companion returns, so it is not actually an immediate pre-mutation verification. Move the charge and exact readback into the companion between confirmation and mutation, or split confirmation from application so a failed charge cannot grant a free, already-reported warp.

title: Validate the newly required companion export
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the newly required companion export**

When the companion DLL is rebuilt and settled without exporting `ShowVv5TimeWarp`, this new lookup always takes `tw_apply_unavailable`, disabling the live Time Warp even though the generated-page regression test still passes because it only finds this export-name string in the executable. The settle script automatically repins the rebuilt DLL, while the patcher's companion export-surface check still lists only the six older exports and therefore accepts that broken artifact. Add `ShowVv5TimeWarp` to the validated companion export surface (preferably by parsing the PE export table) before allowing its identity to be settled.

title: Make settlement independent of checkout line endings
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make settlement independent of checkout line endings**

On an LF checkout, including the repository's current Linux checkout, `raw(ACTIVE)` is `6726AFB4...`, while the checked `ACTIVE_SHA256` is `1983C284...`, the hash of the same JSON with CRLF endings. Because `data/vv5_origins_feature.json` has no enforced EOL attribute, this documented settlement step rewrites the generator and cascades different manifest and identity hashes solely according to `core.autocrlf`; running it again from a Windows checkout produces the other chain. Normalize this input for the raw identity or enforce one checkout representation so the identity chain is reproducible across platforms.

title: Revalidate capacity when the deferred barrel is delivered
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate capacity when the deferred barrel is delivered**

Forcing the random roll to `0x63` requests three children but does not reserve three villager records. Capacity is checked when the player buys the Barrel, while VV1 deliberately waits another 180 update ticks before dispatching it (VV2 waits 90), so if a pregnancy or another event occupies a slot during that interval, the stock per-child allocation can still stop after one or two children despite the full 75,000-point charge. Recheck or reserve all three slots at delivery time before consuming the paid event.

title: Cover helper-derived cave addresses in the VA audit
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cover helper-derived cave addresses in the VA audit**

Fresh evidence beyond the earlier multiline-declaration case is that this broad exception still silently drops nine current VV1 pairs, including `MASK_RESTORE_STUB_FILE_OFFSET`/`MASK_RESTORE_STUB_VA`: their VA expressions call `mask_code_va(...)`, but the evaluator exposes only previously resolved integers, so the call raises and is skipped here. A wrong VA in any of those mask, portrait, save-slot, tick, or newborn caves therefore passes the new audit; the evaluator should safely support this helper-derived form or explicitly require every syntactic offset/VA pair to be accounted for.

title: Paginate the inline-comment query
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Paginate the inline-comment query**

For any PR whose inline review comments span multiple API pages, this command inspects only the first page and can omit later P1 findings. In the inspected GitHub CLI 2.96.0, `gh api --help` defines `--paginate` as making additional requests until there are no more pages; add that flag (and combine its page outputs) so the claimed repository-wide count is not truncated.

title: Request reviews instead of only issue comments
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Request reviews instead of only issue comments**

This command cannot collect the review summaries the surrounding text says were audited: in the inspected GitHub CLI 2.96.0, `gh pr view --help` lists `comments`, `latestReviews`, and `reviews` as separate JSON fields, while the recipe requests only `comments`. Query `reviews`/`latestReviews` or the pull-request reviews API as well, otherwise summaries containing P1 information are absent from the reproduced dataset.

body:
**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update the world-mask nudge documentation**

These constants now move an adult mask 10 px left and 25 px up, so at the documented newborn scale of 0.80 the rounded offsets are 8 px and 20 px. The adjacent implementation comment still claims 4 px and 12 px, and `tests/test_vv3_world_mask_nudge.py` lines 5-12 still describes the reviewed registration as 5/15; anyone using this audit evidence to verify or retune the rendering receives two different specifications, so update both descriptions with the new values.

title: Run source count assertions without local executables
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run source count assertions without local executables**

When the ignored `research/stock-executables` fixtures are absent—as they are in a clean checkout—this calls `skipTest` on the first game and aborts the entire method, even though `_declared` only reads committed source files. Consequently, the advertised cross-game guard never checks VV2 or VV5 counts in that environment; remove the executable prerequisite from this test and leave fixture-dependent verification to `test_the_binaries_roll_the_ranges_this_file_claims`.
